text: Ask the graph "what can I do today?": an assistant for Commons Hub members
description: An LLM over the hub's graph that anyone can ask "what can I do today?" and that answers with a few concrete ideas fitting the person (their interests, time, what is unblocked and valuable), with the path to why each matters. It reads through the read-only MCP (af701cd6), so it cannot damage the graph; picking something up happens in the person's own git account. Related: conversational idea elicitation (0697d033) turns a person's goal into proposed ideas, the reverse direction.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: A read-only tool surface lets anyone use the assistant without write access to the graph.

status.comment: MCP prompt 'today' (packages/mcp/src/prompts.ts; in Claude Code /mcp__aimparency__today, in Claude Desktop from the prompt menu): asks for interests and time if not given, gathers candidates from get_prioritized_ideas, human-dependent/unclear ideas (the ones waiting for a person) and semantic search on interests, and answers with at most three unblocked ideas: title, short id, why it matters (mission path), first step today. Read-only by instruction and by the backend's account access (af701cd6), so guests can use it. No new backend code: any MCP client connected to the hub instance is the assistant. Verified: prompts tests 13/13 (2 new), mcp tsc clean. Not yet tried by a hub member; that depends on the hub instance trial (af701cd6, human-dependent).
